frontmatter_lines.sources: - [Wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheel) (en.wikipedia.org, fetched 2026-10-17) — Ljubljana Marshes wheel and axle (Stare Gmajne, Slovenia) radiocarbon-dated 3340–3030 BCE; two early Neolithic wagon types (circumalpine wheel-and-axle rotating together vs Baden fixed axle), c. 3200–3000 BCE; Sumerian wheeled-wagon pictographs at Uruk c. 3500–3350 BCE; Sintashta culture wooden spoked wheels c. 2000 BCE (Krivoye Lake); iron rim on Celtic chariot wheels in the 1st millennium BCE; Chinese wheel ruts c. 2200 BCE (Pingliangtai) and spoked-wheel hubs 2000–1500 BCE, with west-to-east introduction argued by Rawson/Linduff et al.; Mesoamerican wheeled toys c. 1500 BCE and no practical wheel before the 16th century; llama "not physically suited to use as a draft animal"; Law (1980) *Africa* 50(3) on pre-colonial West African wheeled transport as mostly ceremonial, Chaves–Engerman–Robinson on head porterage as the main method before the colonial period.
frontmatter_lines.topic: mobility as a four-layer material system for fictional cultures — ROUTE (the road and its maintenance institution), VEHICLE (sledge, wheeled cart, litter, watercraft), DRAFT (human porterage, ox, horse, camelid, dog, wind), and WORD (the vehicle vocabulary that travels with the vehicle and outlives it). The master claim: a transport system is three quantities wearing a culture's clothes — payload per unit, terrain law, and clock (how fast a message, an army, or a bride moves) — and the lexicon is evidence of which quantity the culture chose to optimize. Load-bearing cases: the Persian Royal Road (2,699 km Susa–Sardis; courier relay nine days, ninety days on foot; 111 posting stations — [Royal Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Road)); the Roman *cursus publicus* (Augustus's state courier service, Suetonius *Divus Augustus* 49; *mutationes*/mansiones, *diploma* permits, late split into *cursus velox* and *cursus clabularis*; ~50 km/day typical overland — [Cursus publicus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cursus_publicus)); the Inca Qhapaq Ñan (~40,000 km, UNESCO World Heritage 2014; chasqui relay runners, tambo lodges, qullqa warehouses, mita corvée maintenance; llama load ~30 kg at 20 km/day, up to 45 kg short trips — [Inca road system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_road_system)); the Maya sacbeob ("white road"; Coba–Yaxuna ~100 km; *beh* also means "the road of life" and the Milky Way is *sacbe* — [Sacbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacbe)); the Q'eswachaka grass-rope bridge (28 m, renewed annually, UNESCO ICH 2013 — [Queshuachaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queshuachaca)). Secondary claims: wheel history is not a progress ladder (solid disc wheels by the Copper Age; spoked wheels Sintashta c. 2000 BCE; Mesoamerican wheeled toys ~1500 BCE with no practical wheel; West African wheeled vehicles largely ceremonial — [Wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheel)); the harness sequence (ox yoke → breast collar → rigid padded horse collar, with the "horse-collar revolution" as a contested efficiency thesis — [Horse collar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_collar)); the stirrup's late arrival and its "Great Controversy" (White's feudalism thesis vs Bullough/Bachrach — [Stirrup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stirrup)); and the word-travel physics by which vehicle loans outlive vehicles (*coach* < Hungarian *kocsi* "cart of Kocs"; *canoe* < Arawakan *canaoua* via Spanish; *rickshaw* < Japanese *jinrikisha*, English 1879; *junk* < Javanese *djong* via Portuguese *junco*).

frontmatter_lines.topic: the container as a cultural system for fictional cultures — the four load-bearing jobs every vessel inventory answers (COOKING, STORAGE, TRANSPORT, SERVING, plus the ritual/cosmetic/funerary extensions) with real exemplars per job; the six vessel-naming strategies (function, capacity, material, shape, eponym, loan) with attested name families (Greek *krater/amphora/hydria*, Chinese 鼎/簋/壺/瓶/罐, Japanese 甕/壺/鍋/茶碗, English pot/jar/cask); the body-part part-naming grammar (mouth, neck, shoulder, belly, foot) shared by potters' registers cross-linguistically; the container-as-unit metonymy (the container becomes the measure, then the money-word); the ceramic material ladder and the vocabulary each rung generates (earthenware → stoneware → porcelain, plus faience, terracotta, fritware, tin-glaze, celadon) with forming, surface and firing terms; non-ceramic container families (basketry, cooperage, metal, glass, skin, gourd); containers as documents (painted labels, potters' stamps, reign marks — pointed at, not re-covered) and as chronometers (seriation, the period named after a pot); full calibration of the traps (pots≠people, pottery≠farming, the two unrelated wheels, the celadon etymology dispute); a decision-record table; and a build order with one non-canon worked example

Gap filled: the partition already carries *source*-corroboration independence rules (`citation-format-and-source-registry.md:90,192`), one checkpoint-anchoring rule for the provenance ledger (`provenance-audit-ledger-format.md:151`), and a named-reviewer requirement (`verification-method-overview.md:163`) — but no entry states verifier independence (who must not certify what they authored or re-pinned), catalogs the circularity modes this lane has measured, or defines the record that makes a re-pin admissible; the round-8/9 adversarial receipts each discovered one mode in isolation and none was carried into method.

limits: Structural/evidence-presence checks, not quotation truth, historical authenticity or cultural permission. Author-side only; no admission, promotion or canon decision.

Entry discovery uses git (untracked ∪ added-vs-baseline); a staged-only or renamed-existing file is not counted as new. Frontmatter completeness reads the lane's topic/sources/verified-at/recheck/couples profile (QUALITY.md/README); the claim minimum is sources/verified-at/recheck.
The gap check accepts a frontmatter gap field or a body heading/line naming the gap; it verifies that a gap is named, not that the gap is genuine — reviewers own that judgement.
Locator resolvability requires an existing repo path or a URL; bibliographic citations without a path/URL do not count as the retrievable-locator leg.

F command coverage is keyed by script + --flags; positional fixture arguments are not compared, and the inline python3 -c SCORECARD count matches on its JSON target. Cited commands are checked for ledger presence, not re-executed here.
Drift mismatch detection is regex-based over audit.md prose; a positive mismatch reading fails the claim so that it cannot be silently absorbed.

O finding-ID extraction covers the two heading shapes the four source files use (numbered headings and bold F-D17-N markers); findings-17.md's case tables are covered by the row-per-file requirement plus its three F-D17 IDs.
This runner executes no gate, battery or previous-round runner; 'no previously green check regresses' is read through the F ledger rows for those cited commands, not re-measured here.

Calibration controls (disposable, untracked): .scratch/r10x03/make-fixture.py builds a hardlink fixture tree that passes all three claims, and .scratch/r10x03/controls.py plants 18 defects (dropped entry, broken frontmatter, README count/row drift, ledger gaps and silent staleness, audit absence/mismatch, pending or control-less tracker rows, a red scribe, missing verifier files) — each was caught with exit 1 and the expected failure text on 2026-10-17. Scratch is not a deliverable and is not required for this runner to work.

F.coverage_rule: every python3 command cited in SKILL.md and SCORECARD.md, keyed script+flags; --selftest is attributed only to the script its span names (or the single script of a table row)
F.exit_rule: int, or a digit string coerced to int
F.registry_rule: every live tools/gates/*.py named in a drift artifact; registry.md re-measured
F.stale_documented_requires: stated reason >= 12 chars (reason/documented_reason/note/rationale; a literal 'None' placeholder does not count)

O.fixed_rule: control evidence present (existing path or command/exit/sha256/count)
